heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P requires an upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle and extruder gears, along with an enclosure, to safely handle Siraya Tech ABS-GF without extreme wear and warping. With these upgrades in place, it achieves clean functional prints at a safe max print speed of 179 mm/s capped by a 15 mm³/s volumetric flow limit.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + PVP Glue Stick or Liquid Magigoo
slicerTweaks: Cap 'Max volumetric speed' at 15 mm³/s in the Filament Settings to eliminate underextrusion at high feed rates.
Set the Part Cooling Fan to 0% min and 15% max, disabling the auxiliary part cooling fan entirely to prevent delamination.
Add an Outer Brim of 8-10 mm with a 0.0 mm brim-object gap to mechanically anchor sharp corners on the 100°C bed.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' (2 mm) and set Retraction Length to 0.8 mm to counteract glass fiber oozing without grinding the filament.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe bed warping or corner lifting
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Lack of a passive enclosure allows ambient room drafts to cool ABS quickly, inducing severe thermal contraction stress.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install an enclosure around the P1P, preheat the bed to 100°C for 15 minutes before printing, and apply a thin coat of liquid adhesive to the textured PEI plate.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan or draft exposure prevents molten glass-reinforced ABS polymer chains from diffusing across layer boundaries.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off the auxiliary side fan completely, limit part cooling to 0-10% only for overhangs shorter than 3 seconds, and raise nozzle temperature to 265°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking, underextrusion, or rapid nozzle orifice enlargement
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears eroded rapidly by glass fibers, or abrasive grit choked the 0.4mm orifice.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Replace stock components with Bambu Hardened Steel Hotend (0.4mm or 0.6mm) and Hardened Steel Extruder Gears, and verify filament is dried at 80°C for 6 hours.

faq.question: Can I print Siraya Tech ABS-GF on an un-enclosed stock Bambu P1P?
faq.answer: No; printing un-enclosed ABS-GF causes severe delamination and warping from room drafts, and the stock stainless steel nozzle will quickly wear out from glass fibers.

faq.question: What hardware upgrades are strictly required before loading this filament?
faq.answer: You must install the official Bambu Lab Hardened Steel Hotend assembly and Hardened Steel Extruder Gears, along with an enclosure kit or tent.

faq.question: Does Siraya Tech ABS-GF require filament drying before printing?
faq.answer: Yes, ABS-GF is moderately hygroscopic and glass fibers facilitate moisture ingress; dry the spool at 75-80°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing.

faq.question: Why is the print speed capped at 179 mm/s?
faq.answer: At a standard 0.42 mm line width and 0.20 mm layer height, 179 mm/s directly maps to the maximum safe volumetric limit of 15 mm³/s to ensure reliable melting.
